title: Human Resource Management Adventure 2: Recruitment & Training
welcome_lead: Today you'll walk the recruitment process and compare induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training.
meta_desc: Business Management HRM: recruitment process, internal vs external, induction and training types.
final_note: You sequenced recruitment steps and distinguished the three main training methods.

concepts.def: Tasks and duties of the role
Skills and qualities of ideal candidate
Introduction to firm for new hires

walkthroughs.body_html:
Recruitment moves from many applicants to one hire.

1. Identify vacancy → job description (tasks) and person (qualities).
2. Advertise — internally (notice board) or externally (jobsites, agencies).
3. Shortlist applications.
4. Interview, test, reference.
5. Offer and contract.

Internal recruitment: cheaper, faster, motivates staff, but narrows the pool and leaves a gap below.

External recruitment: fresh ideas, wider pool, but costly, slower, and risk of poor cultural fit.

The choice depends on the seniority of the role and the speed required.

Induction — orienting new hires (policies, safety, culture).

On-the-job — shadowing, mentoring, learning live: cheap, relevant, but disruptive and may copy bad habits.

Off-the-job — college courses, external trainers: high quality, transferable skills, but costly and disconnected from the role.
